title: Reading Between the Lines
author: KCC Team
introduction: KCC handles 3500+ emails per week. Most replies address the surface question but miss the emotional or practical need underneath, triggering costly follow-up contacts.
problem: Agents answer what customers wrote, not what they meant. A billing question often hides anxiety about an upcoming disconnection. Addressing only the literal question means the customer comes back.
hypothesis: If AI surfaces the latent intent behind each email and pre-populates a draft that addresses both layers, first-time-right rates will improve significantly.
approach: Claude reads the incoming email plus interaction history, extracts the underlying concern, and generates a draft addressing both the stated and actual question. Agents review, edit, and send.
conclusion: Pilot with 12 agents over 6 weeks: 22% reduction in email repeat contacts and 40% faster drafting time. Expanding to full KCC team Q3 2026.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 1400, "processesAutomated": 1, "impact": "22% fewer repeat email contacts in pilot. 40% faster average draft time."}

title: Full Coverage Quality Control
author: KCC Quality Team
introduction: Quality coordinators can manually review 8% of outgoing emails. That means 92% of customer communications leave without any quality check.
problem: Manual sampling creates blind spots. Issues with tone, accuracy, or compliance surface only after complaints, by which time the damage is done.
hypothesis: An AI scorer running across full email volume lets coordinators focus time on flagged outliers rather than random sampling.
approach: AI scores each outgoing email on clarity, tone, regulatory compliance, and first-time-right likelihood. Emails below threshold are held for human review. Weekly dashboards track quality by agent.
conclusion: Shadow-mode proof-of-concept alongside manual QC shows 84% agreement between AI and human scorers. Full rollout planned Q3 2026.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 800, "processesAutomated": 1, "impact": "Coverage from 8% to near-100%. Coordinator time shifted from sampling to exception review."}

title: Instant Answers in the Moment
author: KCC Platform Team
introduction: Genesys surfaces KB articles during live calls, but agents often bypass it when articles are outdated or too long to scan in real time.
problem: Average handling time spikes when agents hunt for answers manually. KB adoption is low because the content is not trustworthy or fast enough.
hypothesis: Augmenting Genesys KB retrieval with AI reranking and answer synthesis will make the tool fast and accurate enough that agents actually use it.
approach: Claude API integrated with Genesys via CoE architecture. Incoming call context triggers KB search and AI synthesizes a direct answer with source attribution. No Claude seat licence required for frontline agents.
conclusion: Live pilot with 25 agents: AHT down 18 seconds per call. First-contact resolution improved 9 percentage points for calls where KB was consulted. Scaling to 180 agents.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 2600, "processesAutomated": 2, "impact": "AHT minus 18 sec per call. FCR plus 9 points in KB-assisted cohort."}

title: The Always-On Coach
author: KCC Learning Team
introduction: Training 180+ KCC agents is time-intensive and inconsistent. New agents take 6 weeks to reach baseline proficiency and coaching quality depends on individual team leaders.
problem: Trainer capacity limits coaching sessions. Roleplay practice is squeezed into short windows and performance consequences are real.
hypothesis: An always-on AI coach simulating customer conversations and giving instant feedback will cut time-to-proficiency and improve coaching consistency across the team.
approach: LLM-based roleplay simulator trained on anonymised call transcripts and KB content. Agents practice on realistic scenarios and AI scores empathy, accuracy, and resolution rate. Team leaders get weekly analytics.
conclusion: Early access cohort of 20 new agents showed 33% faster time-to-proficiency versus control group. Rolling out to all new hires from Q3 2026.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 3200, "processesAutomated": 3, "impact": "Time-to-proficiency: 6 weeks to 4 weeks. Coaching coverage plus 150%. Coach time freed: 12 hours per week per team leader."}

title: The Grid Intelligence Layer
author: Data & Grid Team
introduction: Budget Thuis processes millions of smart meter readings daily. Hidden in that stream are ghost consumption events, meter drift, and early signs of energy fraud, all invisible to current rule-based checks.
problem: Current anomaly detection flags only obvious outliers. Subtle patterns like a meter consistently under-reading in cold weather or consumption not matching the property profile slip through until a billing dispute surfaces.
hypothesis: An AI model trained on historical reading patterns, weather data, and property profiles can detect subtle anomalies months before they escalate.
approach: Pattern model running on daily meter batches flags readings that deviate from expected behaviour given weather, season, similar-property baseline, and historical trends. High-confidence flags route to the field team.
conclusion: Pilot across 50000 meters detected 340 anomalies in 8 weeks. 67% confirmed as genuine issues versus 31% for the previous rule-based system. Field visit efficiency improved 2.1x.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 4200, "processesAutomated": 5, "impact": "Detection accuracy plus 67% vs rule-based. Field visit efficiency 2.1x. 340 anomalies surfaced in 8-week pilot."}

title: 90 Days Ahead
author: Customer Intelligence Team
introduction: Most churn-prevention efforts kick in after a customer signals intent. By then win-back costs are 5x higher than retention costs.
problem: Churn signals exist in the data weeks before customers consciously decide to leave: complaint frequency, billing confusion patterns, competitive ad exposure. These signals are invisible in siloed systems.
hypothesis: A churn propensity model aggregating cross-system signals 90 days before typical churn enables retention outreach when it is cheapest and most effective.
approach: Feature engineering across CRM, billing, contact history, and external data. Model scores the full customer base weekly. Top-decile at-risk customers trigger personalised retention workflows.
conclusion: Six-month pilot retained 1840 customers who would statistically have churned. Net retention value: 2.3 million euros. Expanding to full base with automated offer generation.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 1200, "processesAutomated": 4, "impact": "1840 customers retained in pilot. EUR 2.3M net retention value. Churn rate in targeted cohort minus 31%."}

title: From Days to Minutes
author: Legal & Procurement Team
introduction: Budget Thuis manages hundreds of supplier and grid operator contracts. Legal review is the bottleneck before any contract can be signed, amended, or disputed.
problem: Junior legal staff spend 60-70% of their time manually extracting key clauses. This is slow, inconsistent, and keeps lawyers from higher-value work.
hypothesis: An AI extraction layer that reads uploaded contracts and structures key clauses will cut review time from days to hours without reducing accuracy.
approach: Claude processes uploaded contract PDFs and extracts 22 predefined clause types including pricing, termination, liability, and force majeure. Flags anomalies versus standard templates and outputs structured JSON.
conclusion: Tested on 43 live contracts: extraction accuracy 91%. Time per contract: 4 days to 40 minutes. AI extraction is now the mandatory first step for all new contracts.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 5800, "processesAutomated": 6, "impact": "4 days to 40 min per contract review. 91% extraction accuracy. Legal capacity freed: 3 FTE-equivalent days per week."}

title: Beat the Inbound Surge
author: Operations & CX Team
introduction: Every major grid outage triggers 300-600 extra contacts to KCC within the first two hours. Agents are overwhelmed and customer frustration compounds the outage experience.
problem: Outage communications take 15-30 minutes to draft and approve, are generic, and are sent after the phones are already ringing.
hypothesis: If AI can generate personalised preapproved outage messages within 3 minutes of a confirmed grid fault, proactive outreach can suppress the inbound surge before it peaks.
approach: Integration with grid monitoring system generates per-customer messages personalised by outage type, estimated resolution time, and product profile. Compliance review happens once on the template.
conclusion: Deployed on 8 major outage events. Inbound surge suppressed by average 58%. Customer satisfaction during outages up 22 points. Rolling out to all future events.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 2100, "processesAutomated": 3, "impact": "Inbound surge suppressed 58%. CSAT during outages plus 22 points. Communication delay: 30 min to 3 min."}

title: Your Usage Your Story
author: Product & Data Team
introduction: Budget Thuis sends 1.2 million customers a generic annual energy summary. Most customers ignore it because it does not tell them anything they could not have guessed.
problem: Generic reports do not drive behaviour change. Customers want to know if they use more than their neighbours and what switching their heating to off-peak would save them.
hypothesis: AI-generated personalised reports comparing usage to a matched peer group and generating specific saving suggestions will increase open rates and drive measurable consumption changes.
approach: Claude generates a unique narrative report per customer segment across 450 micro-segments defined by property type, tenure, product portfolio, and region. Delivered via email with interactive charts.
conclusion: A/B test with 40000 customers: personalised group open rate 61% versus 23% for generic. Average energy reduction in personalised group: 4.2% over following 3 months.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 960, "processesAutomated": 8, "impact": "Open rate: 23% to 61%. Avg consumption reduction 4.2%. Customer effort score plus 18 points for report recipients."}

title: Compliance at the Speed of Regulation
author: Regulatory & Compliance Team
introduction: Dutch energy regulation changes 8-12 times per year in ways that affect Budget Thuis products, pricing, and customer communication. Missing a change means compliance risk or product errors.
problem: Regulatory monitoring is manual: one person reads feeds each morning and flags relevant changes. It is slow, subjective, and relies on no one missing anything.
hypothesis: An AI that monitors regulation feeds daily, classifies changes by relevance, and auto-drafts structured compliance memos will provide better coverage with less effort.
approach: Daily automated fetch of ACM, CBS, ACER, and government gazette feeds. Claude classifies each item by impact area and generates a structured brief with plain-language summary, affected products, and urgency tier.
conclusion: Running 4 months in parallel with manual monitoring. AI surfaced 3 high-impact changes missed by manual review. Zero false-positives required immediate action. Monitoring time reduced by 2.5 hours per day.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 3200, "processesAutomated": 7, "impact": "3 regulation changes surfaced that manual review missed. Monitoring time minus 2.5h per day. Coverage: 5 feeds to 23 feeds."}

title: Trust but Verify
author: Finance Team
introduction: Budget Thuis processes 2400+ supplier invoices monthly. Finance processes them end-to-end but matching each line against contract rates is impractical at volume.
problem: Invoice errors and overbilling go undetected because manual checking is sampled, not comprehensive. Contract terms often differ from invoice formats making line-item matching error-prone.
hypothesis: An AI layer reading invoices against contracts and flagging deviating line items will recover significant value without adding headcount.
approach: Claude processes invoice PDFs alongside relevant contract clauses. Line-item comparison flags discrepancies above defined thresholds. High-confidence anomalies trigger a dispute workflow.
conclusion: Three-month pilot on energy procurement invoices detected 840000 euros in overbilling across 23 suppliers. Average invoice review time: 4 hours to 22 minutes. Coverage now 100% versus previous 12%.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 7200, "processesAutomated": 5, "impact": "EUR 840K overbilling detected in 3-month pilot. Invoice coverage: 12% to 100%. Review time: 4h to 22 min."}

title: Day One Nailed
author: HR & People Team
introduction: Budget Thuis onboards 200+ new employees annually. HR and managers field the same 50 questions every cohort: IT setup, badge access, team norms, benefits, and first-week calendar.
problem: Onboarding quality is inconsistent. Remote new hires get less face-time, managers have variable capacity, and critical information often arrives too late.
hypothesis: An always-on onboarding assistant that knows the employee handbook, benefits guide, and IT setup guide will give instant accurate answers and free HR for higher-value integration activities.
approach: Claude trained on current HR documentation deployed as a conversational interface in Teams. Escalates to HR when questions fall outside the knowledge base or involve sensitive topics.
conclusion: Pilot with 40 new hires across Q1 2026 cohorts: 78% of onboarding questions resolved without HR involvement. Time-to-productivity minus 1.2 weeks versus control. Manager onboarding overhead minus 3.5 hours per new hire.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 5600, "processesAutomated": 2, "impact": "78% questions resolved autonomously. Time-to-productivity minus 1.2 weeks. Manager onboarding overhead minus 3.5h per hire."}

title: Seeing Tomorrow's Load
author: Grid & Energy Trading Team
introduction: Accurate demand forecasting underpins Budget Thuis energy purchasing and balancing positions. Current models miss interaction effects between weather, economic indicators, and customer behaviour.
problem: Forecast errors as small as 2-3% translate into millions in imbalance costs on the day-ahead and intraday markets. Manual model updates lag behind real-world behaviour changes.
hypothesis: A machine learning demand model incorporating weather, economic signals, customer portfolio composition, and recent behaviour patterns will outperform the current model on 48-hour and 7-day horizons.
approach: Ensemble model combining gradient boosting and neural architecture for temporal patterns trained on 4 years of hourly demand data. Outputs: 48h probabilistic forecast, 7-day directional trend, anomaly alerts.
conclusion: Six-week live comparison vs current model: MAE improvement 23% on 48h horizon and 18% on 7-day. Estimated reduction in balancing costs: 1.1 million euros annualised. Handover to grid team for production.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 8800, "processesAutomated": 6, "impact": "MAE minus 23% on 48h forecast. EUR 1.1M annualised balancing cost reduction. 7-day directional accuracy: 91% vs 78% baseline."}

title: Where Time Actually Goes
author: Product & Operations Team
introduction: Budget Thuis runs 14 core customer-facing processes. No one has a complete view of where time goes or where customers drop off because the data is siloed across CRM, billing, and contact systems.
problem: Process improvements are based on intuition and escalations, not data. The same pain points are discussed in quarterly reviews without resolution because the evidence base is thin.
hypothesis: Mining CRM event logs, ticketing data, and call records with AI will surface the precise steps where processes stall and the quick wins with highest impact.
approach: Event log extraction across CRM, billing system, and contact centre. AI identifies process variants, calculates per-step timing, and flags deviations from the intended happy path. Output is a ranked list of bottlenecks.
conclusion: Analysed 6 core processes in 3 weeks. Identified 28 bottlenecks not previously visible. Top 5 fixes estimated to save 14000 handle-minutes per month. First fix in delivery.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 14000, "processesAutomated": 4, "impact": "28 hidden bottlenecks surfaced. 14K handle-minutes per month savings from top-5 fixes. First fix in delivery."}

title: From Source to Socket
author: Energy Product Team
introduction: Follow a single kilowatt-hour on its journey from a wind turbine to a living room — and meet the AI that steers every step of the way.
problem: Between source and socket sit a dozen decisions: how much to buy on the day-ahead market, how to rebalance when the wind forecast shifts, which meters are misreading, and how to explain it all on a bill. Each is handled in a silo, and each silo is a chance for delay and error.
hypothesis: If one intelligence layer watches the whole chain — production forecasts, market prices, grid signals, and customer usage — Budget Thuis can buy sharper, balance cheaper, and tell every customer exactly where their energy came from.
approach: We chained the models end to end. Demand forecasting feeds energy trading. Meter anomaly detection guards the data on the way through the grid. Personalised usage stories close the loop at the socket. Claude orchestrates the handoffs and writes the human-readable layer on top of every link.
conclusion: The chain now runs in production for the full energy portfolio. Forecast-driven purchasing, automated anomaly triage, and personal energy reports share one data spine — the first Budget Thuis product line with AI in every link from source to socket.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 13960, "processesAutomated": 19, "impact": "Every link from source to socket now has an AI co-pilot. EUR 1.1M lower balancing costs. 4.2% lower customer consumption."}

title: A Signal Through the Air
author: Mobile Product Team
introduction: A SIM card is a promise: an invisible signal will find you, wherever you are. This is the story of how AI keeps that promise for every Budget Thuis Sim Only customer.
problem: Mobile is our most personal product but our most anonymous data. Usage spikes, roaming surprises, and bundle mismatches show up as silent dissatisfaction — the customer never calls, they just leave at renewal.
hypothesis: If AI reads the signal — usage patterns, network quality per region, and support contacts — we can fix bundle mismatches and coverage frustrations before the customer ever feels them.
approach: A weekly model scores every SIM on bundle fit and predicts out-of-bundle costs before they happen. Claude drafts proactive bundle advice in plain Dutch. Network complaints are clustered per mast region, so coverage patterns surface in days instead of quarters.
conclusion: Proactive bundle advice reached 38000 customers in the first quarter. Out-of-bundle bill shocks dropped 44%, and churn at renewal in the advised group fell by a quarter. The signal now travels both ways.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 2400, "processesAutomated": 6, "impact": "44% fewer bill shocks. Renewal churn minus 26% in advised group. 38K proactive advice messages in Q1."}

title: Light Through Glass
author: Internet Product Team
introduction: Inside a strand of glass thinner than a hair, light carries a household's whole digital life. Follow the pulse from the exchange to the living room — and the AI tuned to keep it flawless.
problem: When internet stutters, customers experience it instantly but we discover it slowly: modem telemetry, line diagnostics, and contact notes live in three different systems, so most faults are diagnosed only after the customer calls.
hypothesis: The line already tells us when it is sick. If AI reads modem telemetry continuously, we can fix degrading connections before the first buffering wheel appears on a customer's screen.
approach: A model watches line-quality telemetry for every connection and flags the drift patterns that precede faults. Claude turns each flag into a diagnosis with a recommended fix — a channel change, a remote reset, or an engineer visit with the right part already on the van.
conclusion: Six months in: 31% of faults are fixed before the customer notices, first-time-fix on engineer visits is up 19 points, and inbound 'internet down' calls are down by a fifth. Light through glass, watched end to end.
datasection: {"hoursSaved": 5100, "processesAutomated": 7, "impact": "31% of faults fixed before customers notice. First-time-fix plus 19 points. 'Internet down' calls minus 20%."}
